body.statement: For every heavy arm, choose \(J_n\) and the derived \(M_n\) from \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\). Then the deterministic and centered Knight remainders of \(\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}\) converge uniformly on compact local-parameter sets to \(f_a(\tau)t^2/2\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\), \(\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\theta_a=\vartheta_a\), the preliminary quantiles and every wholly empirical drift component are consistent, and \[\left(\frac{n}{h_{a,n}}\{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_a(\tau)\}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}(\tau)}{f_a(\tau)}\right)_{\tau\in\mathcal T}.\] By \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\), the endpoint mark step requires only total-variation convergence of the finite score vector \(\Psi_a(Y(a))\) to \(H_a\); no convergence of the full conditional outcome law is required. The true-propensity fixed-quantile law is recovered by replacing the fitted propensity and empirical clip by their population counterparts.
body.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem, with its transfer condition proved from primitives.
body.gap: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky prove the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile law and no feasible propensity-estimation theorem.
body.consumer: Observational QTE analyses can use flexible assignment models while retaining full-population non-Gaussian calibration.

obligation.what_is_open: After the corrected boundary likelihood expansion is proved, establish joint consistency of the generalized-inverse scale, intermediate Hill statistic, nested preliminary quantiles, endpoint-score ratio, and weighted density estimator, and then complete the finite-vector convex-argmin limit.
obligation.obstruction: The corrected score-transfer inequality controls only the local linear score and Knight curvature. The current core has no uniform likelihood control at the intermediate order \(k_n\), no bandwidth-scale result for the nested quantiles, and no weighted kernel law of large numbers for the fully empirical density. The learner is also formally defective until the proposed construction change is applied.
obligation.attempted: Extended the prior transfer calculation by deriving the effective tail count at the generalized-inverse threshold, the treated count at the Hill threshold, and the exact truncated second-moment order needed by the kernel estimator. These calculations verify that the stated \(k_n\) and bandwidth conditions have the right scale but do not supply the missing likelihood and empirical-process results.
obligation.partial_result:
Assume only for this reduction that the three conclusions of the corrected boundary-likelihood lemma have been established.  The reciprocal identity on the tail band gives, uniformly over the finite set \(\mathcal T\),
\[
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|S^{\mathrm{fe}}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\mathrm{or}}_{a,n}(\tau)|
\le
C E_{a,n}h_{a,n}^{-1}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\]
Hall integration and \(c_an h_{a,n}^{-\gamma_a}\to1\) show that the expectation of the normalized sum is \(O(M_n^{\gamma_a-1})\); truncation gives the same stochastic order.  Thus the right side is
\[
O_P\{E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\]
The same Hall relation gives
\[
nF_a^\pi(1/h_{a,n})\sim h_{a,n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Consequently a uniform relative fitted-propensity error at the sample points, plus the binomial fluctuation of this intermediate count, would imply
\(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\) and
\(h_{a,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1\).

For the Hill threshold \(t_{a,k}=F_a^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\), the Hall expansion gives
\[
t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_a-1)},
\qquad
E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le t_{a,k}\}\right]
\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
This verifies that the stated condition on \(k_n\) is exactly the nonvanishing-denominator condition for the endpoint-score average.  The mark modulus then identifies its population limit as \(m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}\).  Finally,
\[
E\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,n}\}^2}
\right]=O(h_{a,n}^{,2-\gamma_a}),
\]
so the frozen bandwidth condition \(h_{a,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\to0\) is stronger than the variance condition needed by the weighted kernel numerator.  These calculations reduce all empirical centering claims to uniform likelihood control at the extreme and intermediate order statistics, consistency of the nested quantiles on the bandwidth scale, and a uniform kernel law of large numbers.  Those results do not follow from the current frozen nodes, and the present learner must first be corrected before they can be proved.
